Seredne Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Serednie, Ukraine

Not demolished. Presumably established in the 19th century, this cemetery was active at least from 1841 per epigraphic data, used until WWII. Jews are believed to have arrived in the early 18th century; three Jewish families lived there by 1746, growing to 256 by 1830 and 389 (23%) by 1877. Following WWI, the community opened an elementary school for 100 pupils; population reached 599 by 1921 (Czechoslovak period). Jews were integrated into daily town life - 16 artisans, 13 tradesmen, three kosher butchers, plus farmers and professionals. Hungarian forces arrived March 1939, drafting some Jews into forced labor battalions by 1940, with others sent to the Eastern Front where most perished. Population reached 619 by 1941; families without Hungarian citizenship were expelled that year to Kamianets-Podilskyi and murdered. Some Jews fled to the Soviet Union, joining the Czechoslovak army to fight the Nazis on the Eastern Front; the remaining 500 Serednie Jews were marched to the Uzhhorod ghetto, imprisoned for a month and a half before deportation to Auschwitz on May 17, 1944. A few dozen survivors returned postwar but most soon left. No Jews live in the town today.
